newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures fell for the second consecutive day as weakness in the United States, doubts about the likelihood of a stability pact agreement this week and the closing of positions before the yearend weighed on prices.

Analysts said the contract recovered from its lows as some people took the view the selloff had been overdone. Bank of France council member Paul Marchelli also gave the future a boost when he said there was room to cut the intervention rate by up to 50 basis points, without waiting for the Germans.
The December contract settled down 0.40 at 128.30 after touching a low of 127.98 earlier.
"It's clear that we will have difficulty returning to the recent highs before the end of the year, but there isn't any thing which signals a reversal of the trend," a trader said.
Another trader at a French bank said "It's anarchy in this market, don't try and say anything sensible about it...The problem is there are enough variables so no-one really knows what's going on."
"The fact that it's December, however, is a huge factor. At least a third to a half of the activity is from people just saying get me out," he said.

Analysts said it was looking more likely that European finance ministers would fail to come up with a comprehensive pact for keeping overspending governments in line with deficit targets following the introduction of a single currency.
A broad agreement in principle, without progress on the details of pact, would be seen as mildly negative for French bonds while open hostility would be the worst outcome.

"At the other extreme, a complete failure would certainly hit the French fixed income market, raising serious doubts about EMU itself, while raising hopes of devaluation," Eric Chaney, economist at Morgan Stanely, said.

Valerie Plagnol, market economist at Credit Commercial de France said that for any agreement to be received favourably by French bonds it would have to include the "notion of serious recession, and a way to implement it".
"I doubt it would be fully automatic, but it would need to be quick and effective," Plagnol said. "If the agreement's not that different from what's already in Maastricht it's not a stability pact."
March PIBOR suffered during the day with a slightly weaker franc to settle two basis points lower. It got a boost in the GLOBEX session from the Bank of France member's comments.
An analyst at a large French bank in Paris said he did not think the French central bank would lower its intervention rate on Thursday after a regular monetary policy council meeting.
He said the proximity of the Dublin summit, and especially the risk of deadlock, would prompt the Bank of France to adopt a cautious wait and see attitude.
